Class Middlewares

java.lang.Object
forj.http.middleware.Middlewares
public final class Middlewares extends Object
The essential middleware, each generic in F and asking for the least it needs: 
import static forj.http.middleware.Middlewares.*;

HttpApp<IO> app = routes.orNotFound()
        .through(errors())
        .through(timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(10)))
        .through(requestId())
        .through(accessLog());
Each through wraps everything before it, so the last one sees the request first and the response last. With the order above, the access log records the id and the final status, timeouts included, and errors are turned into responses before anything else sees them.

      public static <F> Middleware<F> errors(BiConsumer<Request, Throwable> report, forj.typeclass.MonadError<F, Throwable> errors)
      Turns failures into problem responses (application/problem+json):
      • an HttpFailure (such as a DecodeFailure) answers with its status and its message as the detail;
      • anything else is a 500 whose cause stays private: it goes to report, never to the client.
      Catches both errors raised in F and exceptions a handler throws directly.

      public static <F> Middleware<F> requestId(forj.typeclass.Functor<F> functor)

    • cors

      public static <F> Middleware<F> cors(CorsPolicy policy, forj.typeclass.Applicative<F> ap)
      Cross-origin resource sharing. A preflight (OPTIONS with Access-Control-Request-Method) from an allowed origin is answered here with 204 and never reaches the routes; from another origin, with 403. Other requests from an allowed origin get the Access-Control-* headers added; requests without an Origin, or from origins not allowed, pass through untouched, and the browser withholds the response.
